page: Amazon Web Services x8i.xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor with 4 dedicated vCPUs, mapped to 2 physical cores with hyper-threading. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz and includes a 480 MB L3 cache, alongside 48 KB L1d and 2 MB L2 caches. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 16.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2159.0 and single-threaded gzip compression of 34.54 GB/sec. However, multi-core performance is comparatively weaker, as seen in the stress-ng multi-core score of 4321.66 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 28.77 GB/sec. Memory read bandwidth is also on the lower end, with uncached large block reads at 38.67 GB/sec, though write performance remains average at 29.22 GB/sec. The processor supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions, assisting in workloads like low-parameter LLM inference, where it achieves 592.09 tokens/sec for small model prompt processing.

Given its high memory density of 16 GB per vCPU, the x8i.xlarge offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel CPU scaling. The lack of local storage means storage-heavy operations must rely on network-attached volumes. This instance is well-suited for memory-intensive applications, database operations, caching layers like Redis, and single-threaded data processing tasks.
